title: GitLab and GitHub
intro: Connections to your code forges, made once for the whole workspace: every meeting can read each person's issues through them, and trackers open tickets with them.
instanceHint: Set by the server's variables (GITLAB_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN); without a token, GitHub reads public repositories.
addOwn: Add a connection for this meeting only
addOwnHint: Seen by this meeting alone, for a server or an account the workspace does not have.
connectHint: Your GitLab account, read-only, renewed by itself: no token to copy or to replace when it expires.
name: Name
tokenKept: Leave the token empty to keep the saved one.

tokenHints.gitlab: A personal token with the read_api scope (api for a tracker that opens issues).
tokenHints.github: A fine-grained token that reads issues and pull requests (and writes them, for a tracker that opens issues).

encrypted: Tokens are encrypted before being saved and are never shown again.
noSecretKey: Token encryption is not configured on the server: ask the operators to set the SECRET_KEY key.
removeConfirm: Remove the connection {name}? The meetings using it no longer read through it, and the trackers that open tickets with it are removed.
removeOwnConfirm: Remove the connection {name} of this meeting?

back.failed: Connecting with GitLab failed: try again, or use a personal token.
back.denied: You are not allowed to connect GitLab here.

meeting.title: {kind} connections
meeting.inherited: Until you pick, this meeting uses the workspace's connections.
meeting.picked: This meeting uses the connections ticked below.
meeting.none: No {kind} connection: an administrator can add one to the workspace, or add one for this meeting only below.
meeting.reposHint: “owner/repository” or a whole “owner”, one per line; empty: every repository. Also enter each person's GitHub username in “People and roles”.
meeting.projectsHint: Only issues from these projects are offered for import. Also enter each person's GitLab username in “People and roles”.
